text:
The night was supposed to be about Connor Hellebuyck's return to Winnipeg. Instead the Devils kept him on the bench, Kyle Connor said he was surprised by it, and the two players Winnipeg got back in the Hellebuyck trade decided the game. Dawson Mercer scored twice against his old team and Nico Daws made 19 saves against his, and the Jets beat New Jersey 4-2 for their fourth straight win. The Devils' five-game winning streak is over.

Mercer's first goal was the least likely of the night: a wrist shot with a 2% chance of going in, 7:54 into the game, set up by Cole Perfetti. Connor made it 2-0 on a power play later in the first, with Perfetti and Mark Scheifele assisting. New Jersey answered fast at the start of the second, Jesper Bratt and Cody Glass scoring 44 seconds apart, the Glass goal a tip-in off a Johnathan Kovacevic shot. For most of the second period the Devils had the better of it.

The third belonged to Winnipeg, 1.8 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 0.63. Mercer won it on a power play at 11:58, the goal that moved the Jets' win chance from 53% to 85%, and by our count it added nearly half a win on its own. Daws made his biggest save soon after, on Luke Evangelista, and Connor hit the empty net with 58 seconds left. Connor had seven shots and 1.5 expected goals on his own stick, and his line controlled play whenever it was out.

On the whole the game was even. New Jersey had more shot attempts, even-strength chances were dead level, and by our replay of every shot the Devils deserved this one 51% of the time. Special teams split it: Winnipeg went 2 for 4 on the power play, New Jersey 0 for 4. Jake Allen allowed three goals on 24 shots in Hellebuyck's place, 0.6 worse than expected.

The Devils will see the Jets again, and so will Hellebuyck. Whatever the reason he sat, Winnipeg got to enjoy a night where its side of the trade looked very good.
headline: Hellebuyck sits, and the trade's other half wins it
